1.explanation:
• DataTable/README.md explains the intended markup and CSS classes for selectable rows, so we can compare expected vs. actual.
• DataTable/migrate-to-7.x.md highlights recent changes to DataTable markup that might have dropped the wrapper class.
• DataTable/state/TableSelection.js contains the getSelectionProps logic that drives the <TableSelectRow> rendering—where the <td> wrapper class should be applied.
• DataTable/stories/DataTable.stories.js shows the live example of selectable rows in Storybook; it reproduces the missing-class scenario.
• src/components/DataTable/TableSelectRow.js is the component source where the <td> and its className should be added.
• DataTable/tools/buildTableProps.js may generate cell props (including class names) for table columns—if the wrapper class is omitted here it never reaches the markup.
1.bug_scenario: When using the React carbon‐components DataTable with selectable rows (<TableSelectRow>), the <td> wrapper around the checkbox input is rendered without the “bx--table-column-checkbox” class. On the official Carbon site the selectable‐row cells have that class (so rows render at 48px height), but in the React component the missing class makes each row render at 52px—breaking alignment and styling.
